newsitem.title: GERMANY: German firms launch online service for the blind.
newsitem.headline: German firms launch online service for the blind.

text.p: A group of German companies said on Monday they planned to launch an online computer service that would provide news and information for the blind.
The service -- dubbed "Cityweb plus" -- would cost 40 marks a month and deliver news and information over the Internet in text form to a brail display linked to a personal computer.
The service was developed by an industry consortium including publisher Westdeutsche Allgemeine Zeitung (WAZ), computer maker Siemens Nixdorf and media giant Bertelsmann.
The companies plan to unveil the service on Tuesday at a conference on electronic commerce for small and mid-sized companies sponsored by the Group of Seven industrial nations and hosted by Germany.

The service is expected to become operational later this year. The companies plan to introduce a text-to-speech enhancement that would read news and electronic mail aloud to blind PC users in the autumn.
Wolfgang Kitza, chairman of Telemedia, the Bertelsmann subsidiary responsible for the project, said there were around 155,000 blind people in Germany, of which 12,000 work on computers.
